releases.notes: the screen and the volume follow a knob without the delay: the screen redraws only what changed, a fast turn moves all the way at once, and a volume change lands at once. A knob set to Games follows the games Polaris for desktop sees running (Polaris for desktop 0.1.134 or later).

on Windows, setting up Polaris' driver shows only the Windows permission prompt, with no window behind it. Polaris lets go of the Stream 100 while its driver goes on and restarts it on the new driver, so the knobs work right after; if Windows needs a restart first, the page says so. With Polaris' driver in use, the page no longer offers to open Hercules Stream Control.

on Windows, an install from before the driver was part of it gets Polaris' driver by itself on the next start or update, with one Windows permission prompt. The page says the driver is being set up instead of asking you to install it; only if the prompt was declined or the setup failed does it say why, next to a Set up the driver button.

the screen speaks the app's language, English or Spanish with its accents. "People in the call" shows your Polaris call: how many are in it, your microphone and sound, and who is speaking or muted. "What is playing" shows the song or video playing on Windows or Linux; macOS does not let apps read it, so there the screen shows the knobs.

on macOS 14.2 and later the knobs set to calls, music, games or the browser set those apps' volume, as on Windows and Linux; the install asks once to let Polaris record system audio, which macOS needs for it, and the page offers it again if the answer was no. Before macOS 14.2 the page says per-app volume needs 14.2; the whole output works.

works on Linux and macOS, on x64 and Arm alike, and on Windows on Arm. On Linux the install asks once, together with the permissions, to let Polaris open the Stream 100 (one password prompt), and puts that back by itself if it goes missing. On macOS the knobs set the whole output's volume; a knob set to one kind of app does nothing there yet.
its status sentences ship with the plugin, in English and Spanish, so a new version of it no longer needs a Polaris update to say them.
with Polaris' own driver the controller's screen shows what each knob controls and its volume, muted ones in red, at the brightness set here; "Off" turns it off.

a turn of a knob moves the volume about half way, instead of needing five full turns from silent to full, whether the controller is read through the Hercules software or Polaris' own driver. The page says plainly that Polaris does not draw on the controller's screen yet.

on Windows the driver is part of the install: the install asks once, together with the permissions, and Polaris puts its own driver on the Stream 100 with one Windows permission prompt, and puts it back by itself when the Stream 100 comes back with another one. The "Polaris driver on this PC" switch is gone.
called a device plugin instead of an add-on; nothing else changed.

works with no Hercules software: turning on "Polaris driver on this PC" (one Windows permission prompt) puts Polaris' own driver on the Stream 100, turning it off puts the previous one back, and uninstalling the plugin puts the previous driver back. The knob presses follow the printed numbers.
the knobs and lit buttons are read through the Hercules software from the Polaris app too, not only when tested on their own; before, the status said Polaris could not read the Stream 100 through it.

the knobs and lit buttons work with the Hercules software installed: Polaris reads them through it while Hercules Stream Control is closed, and the status says to close it while it is open. Pressing a knob no longer nudges its volume.
the status says plainly why the Stream 100 cannot be read, in English and Spanish (0.1.4 shipped twice, and the first one kept the old wording).

the knobs, the lit buttons, how the knobs turn and the screen are set on the plugin's page with Polaris's own controls, laid out as the controller, in English and Spanish; above them, a preview of what the screen shows.
an editor on the plugin's page shows the controller - what the screen shows, each knob and each lit button - and changes them in place.

each knob follows calls, music, games, the browser or the whole output, with steady steps and no jumps; the lit buttons mute, deafen, turn the camera on or off, or leave the call. Reads the controller on Windows once Windows' own driver is in use, and on Linux where the system lets Polaris open it.
